reason: This passage (Exodus 1:15-22) describes the Pharaoh's command to the Hebrew midwives and their response. It contains no reference to Yahweh's anger being triggered by people voicing opinions or feelings. Instead, the text states that the midwives 'feared God' (וַתִּירֶאן אֶת־ הָאֱלֹהִים) and that 'God was good to the midwives' (וַיֵּיטֶב אֱלֹהִים לַֽמְיַלְּדֹת). There is no instance of Yahweh hearing people express their opinions and responding with anger. The passage shows God favoring those who feared Him and acted righteously, but provides no support for the stated claim.
